sbh2.0:2.53: The person whose faculties are not slow-functioning,
sbh2.0:2.55: in [their relation to] the knowable entity — as before.

sbh2.0:2.57: [one sharp] from the beginning [by virtue of] sharp-faculty lineage,
sbh2.0:2.58: and [one sharp because his] faculties [are] cultivated.
sbh2.0:3.2: The person by whom, in previous other births, lust was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of — he, by that cause, by that condition, now has intense lust and prolonged lust toward a lust-arousing thing.
sbh2.0:3.3: This is called the lust-intoxicated person.
sbh2.0:3.5: The person by whom, in previous other births, hatred was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of —
sbh2.0:3.6: by that cause, by that condition, [he] now has intense hatred and prolonged hatred toward a hatred-arousing thing.
sbh2.0:3.10: The person by whom, in previous other births, delusion was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of —
sbh2.0:3.11: by that cause, by that condition,
sbh2.0:3.12: [he] now has intense delusion and prolonged delusion toward a delusion-arousing thing. This is called the delusion-intoxicated person.
sbh2.0:3.14: The person by whom, in previous other births, conceit was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of — by that cause, by that condition,
sbh2.0:3.15: [he] now has intense conceit and prolonged conceit toward a conceit-arousing thing.
sbh2.0:4.1: This is called the conceit-intoxicated person.
sbh2.0:4.3: The person by whom, in previous other births, applied thought was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of — by that cause, by that condition, [he] now has intense applied-thought and prolonged applied-thought toward an applied-thought-arousing thing.
sbh2.0:5.2: The person by whom, in previous other births, lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought were not resorted to, cultivated, [or] made much of, and [for whom] these dharmas were not seen as dangerous,
sbh2.0:5.4: he, by that cause, by that condition, in a lust-arousing or hatred-arousing [Lacuna] or conceit-arousing or applied-thought-arousing thing, does not have intense lust,
sbh2.0:5.6: and lust does not become manifest in him through that thing.
sbh2.0:5.7: As with lust, so with hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought.
sbh2.0:5.8: This is called the balanced person.
sbh2.0:5.10: The person by whom, in previous other births, lust was not resorted to, [not] made much of,
sbh2.0:5.11: and [who] has often seen it as dangerous,
sbh2.0:5.12: found fault with it, thoroughly examined it —
sbh2.0:5.13: he, by that cause, by that condition, now toward a lust-arousing thing [that is] encountered, present, strong, abundant, [and] glaring, produces [Conjectural: slight] lust;
sbh2.0:5.14: toward a middle or small one, he does not produce [it].
sbh2.0:5.15: As with lust, so with hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought are to be understood.
sbh2.0:5.16: This is called the slight-dust person.

sbh2.0:9.2: The person who, in the dharmas as heard, mastered, reflected on,
sbh2.0:9.4: fit to follow those dharmas by way of cultivation, [and]
sbh2.0:10.1: does not seek instruction-and-admonition from another,
sbh2.0:10.2: namely, for the attainment of the [path-]fruit — this is called the dharma-follower person.
sbh2.0:10.5: at the moment when he attains [Conjectural: the recluse-fruit],
sbh2.0:10.8: by the path of instruction-and-admonition from another — at that moment he is called faith-resolved.
sbh2.0:11.3: that very dharma-follower person, at the moment when he attains the recluse-fruit,
sbh2.0:11.6: — at that moment he is called view-attainer.
sbh2.0:12.3: attains the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*) in forward and reverse order,
sbh2.0:12.4: and rises out [of them], and, having realized [them] with the body, dwells much [therein], but does not entirely attain the destruction of the fluxes — this is called the body-witness person.
sbh2.0:13.2: This person, by the abandonment of the three fetters — personality-view (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), clinging-to-virtue-and-vow (*śīlavrata-parāmarśa*), [and] doubt (*vicikitsā*) — becomes a stream-enterer,
sbh2.0:13.3: of non-falling nature, certain, bound for awakening.
sbh2.0:13.4: [As] one whose maximum is seven times,
sbh2.0:13.5: [after] seven times transmigrating among the gods and humans, he makes an end of suffering. [Lacuna]
sbh2.0:13.6: Both are to be understood as stream-enterer persons.
sbh2.0:13.7: Now, what is the one-interval person (*ekavīcika*)?
sbh2.0:13.8: The once-returner person practicing for the fruit of non-returning, for whom the strong and middling realm-of-desire defilements are abandoned,
sbh2.0:13.10: and, having produced only one realm-of-desire existence, there itself he attains final nirvāṇa.
sbh2.0:13.11: He once returns to this [world] — this is called the one-interval [one].
sbh2.0:14.5: just upon decease, at the time of intermediate-existence-generation, [he] generates the intermediate existence and at the very moment of generation attains final nirvāṇa —
sbh2.0:14.6: like a small spark of fire, which, when arisen, is at once extinguished.
sbh2.0:14.8: having generated the intermediate existence, [and] standing there some time after the generation, after some time attains final nirvāṇa —
sbh2.0:14.9: but not [so that] he has [Conjectural: approached] where the rebirth-existence is —
sbh2.0:14.10: like an iron spark that flies out from [Conjectural: iron lumps] or iron plates, heated glowing and beaten with iron hammers — so he attains final nirvāṇa.
sbh2.0:14.11: The third in-between-nirvāṇa person: having generated the intermediate existence, he approaches [the place] where the rebirth-existence [will be],
sbh2.0:14.12: and, having approached, [but] not yet reborn, attains final nirvāṇa —
sbh2.0:14.14: an iron-spark that has flown out [and], before falling on the earth,
sbh2.0:14.16: These three intermediate-existence-nirvāṇa persons, gathered into one, are called the in-between-nirvāṇa person.
sbh2.0:14.18: He who, just upon being reborn, attains final nirvāṇa.
sbh2.0:15.2: He who, reborn there, brings the path into presence without effort, without exertion, without exhaustion, and attains final nirvāṇa — this is called the without-effort-nirvāṇa person.
sbh2.0:15.4: He who, reborn there, brings the path into presence with effort, with exertion, with exhaustion, and attains final nirvāṇa — this is called the with-effort-nirvāṇa person.

sbh2.0:17.2: This is called the upstream-goer person.
sbh2.0:17.4: The mild-faculty-lineage person who falls back from the worldly seen-dharma pleasure-dwellings (*dṛṣṭa-dharma-sukha-vihāra*),
sbh2.0:17.6: or protects [his] liberation, [having] fallen into intense fear of heedlessness;
sbh2.0:17.7: namely, taking that very [tendency to] falling-back as predominant, [only] that much is his wholesome side,
sbh2.0:17.8: and, through the passing of those nights and days, moments, instants, [and] hours, he does not greatly proceed to distinction,
sbh2.0:17.9: so long as he does not make intense effort.
sbh2.0:17.10: This is called the sometimes-liberated person.
sbh2.0:18.2: By the reverse of [the above], the unshakable-dharma person is to be understood.
sbh2.0:19.2: The person who entirely attains the destruction of the fluxes,
sbh2.0:19.3: but does not dwell, having attained, realizing the eight liberations with the body.
sbh2.0:19.4: This is called the wisdom-liberated person.
sbh2.0:19.6: The person who entirely attains the destruction of the fluxes [and]
sbh2.0:19.7: dwells having attained the eight liberations with the body.
sbh2.0:19.8: His mind is liberated from the obstacle of defilement (*kleśa-āvaraṇa*)
sbh2.0:19.9: and from the obstacle to liberation (*vimokṣa-āvaraṇa*) — this is called the both-ways-liberated person.
sbh2.0:20.1: What is the delineation of persons?
sbh2.0:20.2: The delineation of persons is to be understood by eleven divisions.
sbh2.0:20.3: By which eleven? Namely: by division of faculty, by division of community (*nikāya*), by division of conduct, by division of vow, by division of practice, by division of path-fruit, by division of application,
sbh2.0:20.4: by division of attainment, by division of rebirth, by division of falling-back, [and] by division of obstacle.
sbh2.0:21.2: [there is] the delineation of mild-faculty and sharp-faculty persons.
sbh2.0:22.1: By division of community (*nikāya*), the delineation of seven kinds of person:
sbh2.0:22.2: monk, nun, female probationer, male novice, female novice, layman, laywoman.
sbh2.0:23.1: Now, by division of conduct, the delineation of seven persons:
sbh2.0:23.2: he who is the lust-intoxicated person is lust-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.3: he who is hatred-intoxicated is hatred-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.4: he who is delusion-intoxicated is delusion-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.5: he who is conceit-intoxicated is conceit-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.6: he who is applied-thought-intoxicated is applied-thought-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.7: the balanced person (*samaprāpta*) is even-balanced in conduct;
sbh2.0:23.8: the slight-dust person (*mandarajaska*) is slight in conduct — [thus they are] to be understood.
sbh2.0:24.1: Now, what are the marks of the lust-conducted person?
sbh2.0:24.2: Here the lust-conducted person, [even] toward a slight, wholly inferior lust-arousing thing, produces a dense, strong lust-obsession —
sbh2.0:24.3: what more toward a middle or fine [thing]?
sbh2.0:24.4: And that lust-obsession he maintains in continuity for a long time,
sbh2.0:24.5: [remains] bound [by it] for a long time.
sbh2.0:24.6: Through that obsession, he is overcome by lust-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:24.7: but he is not able to overcome the lust-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:24.8: He is of smooth faculties, not of stiff faculties,
sbh2.0:24.9: [Conjectural: not] of rough faculties, not of [Conjectural: coarse] faculties;
sbh2.0:24.10: not too much harming others — namely by body or by speech; [yet he is] hard to detach, hard to stir;
sbh2.0:24.16: magnanimous; greedy by nature for requisites and provisions, giving great weight to them; full of joy, full of delight, free from frowning, of open-faced complexion, accompanied by a smile — these and the like are to be understood as the marks of the lust-conducted person.
sbh2.0:24.17: What are the marks of the hatred-conducted person?
sbh2.0:24.19: toward a hatred-arousing thing, [even] by a slight sign of an aversion-provoking thing (*pratigha-vastu-nimitta*), produces a dense, abundant aversion-obsession —
sbh2.0:24.20: what more by a middle or strong [one]?
sbh2.0:24.21: And that aversion-obsession he maintains in continuity for a long time,
sbh2.0:24.22: [remains] bound [by it] for a long time.
sbh2.0:24.24: he is overcome by hatred-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:24.25: but cannot overcome the hatred-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:24.27: of stiff faculties, of rough faculties, of coarse faculties, and is excessively harming others by nature —
sbh2.0:24.28: namely by body and by speech.
sbh2.0:24.29: Yet he is easy to detach,
sbh2.0:24.33: not firm in undertakings, not steady in undertakings;
sbh2.0:24.34: not of firm vow, not of stable vow;
sbh2.0:24.35: full of dejection, full of distress;
sbh2.0:24.38: one who takes things the wrong way, hard to bring around, full of grudges;
sbh2.0:24.39: of cruel intent, fierce, taking offense, replying word-for-word — even when slightly addressed, he is offended,
sbh2.0:24.45: of non-open face, hating others’ fortune, full of envy — these and the like are to be understood as the marks of the hatred-conducted person.
sbh2.0:25.1: Now, what are the marks of the delusion-conducted person?
sbh2.0:25.2: Here the delusion-conducted person, [even] toward a slight delusion-arousing thing, produces a dense, abundant delusion-obsession —
sbh2.0:25.3: [and] still more toward a middle or strong [thing]; and he maintains the continuity of that delusion-obsession for a long time,
sbh2.0:25.5: He is overcome by delusion-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:25.6: but cannot overcome the delusion-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:25.9: of intoxicated faculties, of loose bodily action; an ill-thought-thinker, ill-speech-speaker, ill-deed-doer; lazy, not endowed with [the capacity for] rising;
sbh2.0:25.13: a wrong-grasper, hard to detach, hard to stir, of inferior conviction;
sbh2.0:25.14: born deaf-mute, [Conjectural: speaking by hand signs],
sbh2.0:25.16: to understand the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken [teachings], and by nature led along by conditions,
sbh2.0:25.17: other-led, other-driven — these and the like are to be understood as the marks of the delusion-conducted person.
sbh2.0:26.1: Now, what are the marks of the conceit-conducted person?
sbh2.0:26.2: Here the conceit-conducted person, [even] toward a slight conceit-arousing thing, produces a dense conceit-obsession —
sbh2.0:26.3: what more toward a middle or strong [one]?
sbh2.0:26.4: And the continuity of that conceit-obsession he maintains for a long time,
sbh2.0:26.9: He is overcome by conceit-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:26.10: but cannot overcome the conceit-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:26.11: He is of restless faculties, of elevated faculties; engaged in adorning the body, he speaks an excessively haughty speech, not lowered [in tone]; and toward [Conjectural: parents,] teachers and those in the place of teacher he does not, from time to time, pay the proper respect.
sbh2.0:26.13: of unbowed body, not given to salutation, bowing, rising, joined palms, and proper service; self-grasping, self-exalting, other-deprecating;
sbh2.0:26.14: desirous of gain, desirous of honor, desirous of fame, voice, [and] eulogy;
sbh2.0:26.15: frivolous, given to jesting, [Conjectural: hard to detach],
sbh2.0:26.16: hard to stir, of lofty inclination,
sbh2.0:26.18: and is full of strong views of self, being, soul, nourisher, person, and individual, and of resentment,
sbh2.0:26.19: and full of grudges — these and the like are to be understood as the marks of the conceit-conducted person. Now, what are the marks of the applied-thought-conducted person?
sbh2.0:26.20: Here the applied-thought-conducted person, [even] toward a slight applied-thought-arousing thing, produces a dense obsession,
sbh2.0:26.21: and that obsession he maintains for a long time,
sbh2.0:26.23: He is overcome by applied-thought-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:26.24: but cannot overcome the applied-thought-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:26.30: [Conjectural: erring in verbal action]; hard to detach, hard to stir; fond of [conceptual] proliferation (*prapaṁca*), delighting in proliferation;
sbh2.0:26.31: full of doubt, full of indecision;
sbh2.0:26.32: and of varied desire, of unstable vow,
sbh2.0:26.36: full of suspicion, of lost mindfulness;
sbh2.0:26.37: non-delighting in seclusion, full of distraction;
sbh2.0:26.39: skilful, not lazy — these and the like are to be understood as the marks of the applied-thought-conducted person.
sbh2.0:27.1: This is the delineation of persons by division of conduct, [thus] to be understood.
sbh2.0:28.1: Now, the delineation of persons by division of vow (*praṇidhāna*):
sbh2.0:28.2: there is a person who has made his vow in the disciple-vehicle,
sbh2.0:28.3: there is one in the solitary-buddha-vehicle,
sbh2.0:28.4: [and] there is one in the great vehicle.
sbh2.0:28.6: who has made his vow in the disciple-vehicle may be of disciple-lineage, may be of solitary-buddha-lineage,
sbh2.0:28.8: [Likewise,] this person who has made his vow in [the path of] solitary awakening may also be of solitary-buddha-lineage, of disciple-lineage, [or] of great-vehicle-lineage.
sbh2.0:28.9: [And] this person who has made his vow in the great vehicle may also be of disciple-lineage, may be of solitary-buddha-lineage, [or] may be of great-vehicle-lineage.
sbh2.0:28.10: [Now,] this disciple-lineage person who has made his vow in solitary awakening or in supreme perfect awakening —
sbh2.0:28.11: he, on account of his disciple-lineage, necessarily at the final time will turn back that vow and stand only in the disciple-vehicle vow.
sbh2.0:28.12: Thus the solitary-buddha-lineage and great-vehicle-lineage [persons] are to be understood.
sbh2.0:28.13: For these persons there is accumulation of the vow and alteration of the vow,
sbh2.0:28.14: but no accumulation of lineage or alteration of lineage.
sbh2.0:28.15: In this context, these persons are to be understood as of disciple-vehicle vow and of disciple-lineage.
sbh2.0:29.1: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of vow.
sbh2.0:30.1: How is the delineation of persons by division of practice (*pratipat-prabheda*)?
sbh2.0:30.2: Of these persons just pointed out [and] proclaimed, [their] going forth is by four practices.
sbh2.0:30.4: There is the painful practice with slow knowledge;
sbh2.0:30.5: there is the painful practice with quick knowledge;
sbh2.0:30.6: there is the pleasant practice with slow knowledge; [and] there is the pleasant practice with quick knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.1: Of the mild-faculty person [Conjectural: who has not attained the basic dhyāna], the practice is called painful, with slow knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.2: Of the sharp-faculty person [Conjectural: who has not attained the basic dhyāna], the practice is called painful, with quick knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.3: Of the mild-faculty person who has attained the basic dhyāna (*mauladhyāna*), the practice is called pleasant, with slow knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.4: Of the sharp-faculty person who has attained the basic dhyāna, the practice is called pleasant, with quick knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.5: Thus the delineation of persons by division of practice is to be understood.
sbh2.0:32.1: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of path-fruit to be understood?
sbh2.0:32.3: of the four practitioners — practitioner for the fruit of stream-entry, of once-returning, of non-returning, [and] of arhatship — and of the four fruit-attainers — stream-enterer, once-returner,
sbh2.0:32.4: non-returner, [and] arhat — and of those for whom the practitioner-paths [still] proceed:
sbh2.0:32.5: they are practitioners; their delineation is by the practitioner-path.
sbh2.0:32.6: Those established in the recluse-fruits, [up to] the arhat-fruit — their delineation is by the path-fruit. Thus is the delineation of persons by division of path-fruit.
sbh2.0:33.1: How is the delineation of persons by division of application?
sbh2.0:33.2: Namely, by [the categories of] faith-follower and dharma-follower.
sbh2.0:33.3: The person who is applied [to the path] by faith-following
sbh2.0:33.4: is the faith-follower; the one applied to the dharmas by following a discipline [Conjectural: not] dependent on another’s condition is the dharma-follower.
sbh2.0:33.5: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of application.
sbh2.0:33.6: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of attainment (*samāpatti*)?
sbh2.0:33.7: Namely, of the body-witness, who, having realized the eight liberations with the body, dwells having attained [them],
sbh2.0:33.8: and does not entirely attain the destruction of the fluxes.
sbh2.0:33.10: Inwardly with non-form perception, [yet] externally he sees forms.
sbh2.0:33.11: He realizes the pure liberation with the body and dwells having attained [it].
sbh2.0:33.12: The sphere of infinite space, of infinite consciousness, of nothingness, of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the cessation of perception-and-feeling he attains and rises out of, in forward and reverse order.
sbh2.0:33.13: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of attainment.
sbh2.0:33.14: How is the delineation of persons by division of rebirth?
sbh2.0:33.16: Namely, [the delineation] of the seven-times-at-most, of the family-to-family, of the one-interval, of the in-between-nirvāṇa, of the upon-rebirth-nirvāṇa, [Lacuna] [and] of the upstream-goer.
sbh2.0:33.17: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of rebirth.
sbh2.0:33.18: How is the delineation of persons by division of falling-back [and non-falling-back]?
sbh2.0:33.20: Namely, of the sometimes-liberated arhat, who is liable to fall back from the pleasant dwellings of the present life; and the delineation by the division of non-falling-back [is]
sbh2.0:34.1: of the unshakable arhat, who is not liable to fall back from the pleasant dwellings of the present life.
sbh2.0:34.2: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of falling-back [and non-falling-back].
sbh2.0:34.3: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of obstacle (*āvaraṇa*)?
sbh2.0:34.4: Namely, of the wisdom-liberated and both-ways-liberated arhats.
sbh2.0:34.5: The wisdom-liberated arhat is liberated from the obstacle of defilement, [but] not from the obstacle of attainment (*samāpatti-āvaraṇa*);
sbh2.0:34.8: is liberated from the obstacle of defilement and from the obstacle of attainment — therefore he is called both-ways-liberated.
sbh2.0:34.9: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of obstacle. — By these three divisions, as pointed out, the delineation of the persons as pointed out is, in order, to be understood.
sbh2.0:35.3: The grossness of the lower planes: namely, [that] of the realm of desire relative to the first dhyāna, and so on up to [that of the sphere of nothingness relative to] the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
sbh2.0:35.4: What, in this context, is grossness?
sbh2.0:35.6: grossness in essential nature (*svabhāva-audārika*), and grossness in number/quantity (*saṁkhyā-audārika*).
sbh2.0:35.7: As for grossness in essential nature: in the realm of desire the five aggregates are [also] present,

sbh2.0:37.1: Now, what is the truth of suffering?
sbh2.0:37.2: Namely: birth is suffering, aging too is suffering, illness [is suffering], death [is suffering], union with the unloved [is suffering], separation from the loved [is suffering], and frustration of desire [is suffering] —
sbh2.0:37.3: in short, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering.
sbh2.0:37.4: The noble truth of origin is craving — productive of further existence, bound up with delight and lust, taking delight here and there.
sbh2.0:38.1: The noble truth of cessation is the complete abandonment of that very craving.
sbh2.0:39.1: The truth of the path is the noble eightfold path.
sbh2.0:39.2: The fourfold delineation of [these] truths is made by reference to the dark side and the bright side, by the structure of cause and effect:
sbh2.0:40.1: the truth of suffering is the effect,
sbh2.0:40.2: the truth of origin is the cause [on the dark side];
sbh2.0:40.3: the truth of cessation is the effect,
sbh2.0:40.4: the truth of the path is the cause [on the bright side] — for the attainment, for the direct touching [of cessation].
sbh2.0:40.5: The truth of suffering is like the illness: it is to be fully known first.
sbh2.0:40.6: The truth of origin is like the cause of the illness:
sbh2.0:40.7: it is to be discarded next.
sbh2.0:40.8: The truth of cessation is like health:
sbh2.0:40.9: it is to be touched, to be realized directly.
sbh2.0:40.10: The truth of the path is like the medicine:
sbh2.0:40.11: it is to be resorted to, to be cultivated,
sbh2.0:40.13: And [each] is real, just so, not otherwise, not contradicted, not perverted: suffering by way of being suffering, [and so on] up to the path by way of being the path — therefore [each] is called a truth.
sbh2.0:40.14: And its specific characteristic does not deceive,

sbh2.0:40.16: For that reason it is called truth.
sbh2.0:40.17: Why, again, are these truths only of the noble ones (*ārya*)?

sbh2.0:89.26: Now, the good worldlings who have entered upon practice for their own benefit —
sbh2.0:89.28: applied for the attainment of the not-yet-attained, for the reaching of the not-yet-reached, for the direct realization of the not-yet-realized; fit and capable, [and so on] up through [their being capable of] the direct realization of the not-yet-realized.
sbh2.0:89.29: These are called those who live by the path.
sbh2.0:89.30: In them there is warmth for the arising of this noble wisdom-faculty; they are not dead, but are said to be alive.
sbh2.0:89.31: Therefore they are called those who live by the path.
sbh2.0:89.32: Now, that person who is of bad virtue, of evil dharma, [and so on] up through [the formula] ‘non-celibate, claiming to be celibate,’
sbh2.0:89.33: he is called defiler of the path — by him the path is defiled from the root, from the beginning,
sbh2.0:89.34: by which he becomes unfit, incapable,
sbh2.0:89.35: a non-vessel for the arising of the path,
sbh2.0:89.36: even though the teaching of the path exists, even though realization is present.
sbh2.0:89.37: Therefore he is called defiler of the path.

sbh2.0:93.13: Or [Damaged] — knower of means, skilful: that is the meaning.
sbh2.0:93.14: Application on the side of continuity, continuous, alert — so it is called.
sbh2.0:93.15: Long cultivated [Damaged] by the threefold distinction,

sbh2.0:93.25: And who is of ripe faculties, knower of means,

sbh2.0:94.1: Now, the four māras and the many māra-actions
sbh2.0:94.2: are to be understood by the yogin
sbh2.0:94.4: and, having been fully known, they should be avoided.
sbh2.0:94.6: namely, the aggregate-māra (*skandha-māra*), the defilement-māra (*kleśa-māra*), the death-māra (*maraṇa-māra*),
sbh2.0:94.8: The five aggregates of clinging are the aggregate-māra.
sbh2.0:94.9: The defilements ranging in the three realms [are the defilement-māra].
sbh2.0:94.10: The death, the dying, of these and those beings
sbh2.0:94.11: from this and that group of beings is the death-māra.
sbh2.0:94.12: And the deva-son born in the realm of desire who, for one engaged on the [Conjectural: wholesome] side in passing beyond the aggregates, the defilements and death,
sbh2.0:94.17: and that which is death, and that by which one is made to yield to death, [and that which] turns [one] aside by an obstructive thing —
sbh2.0:94.18: by reference to this, the four māras are established.
sbh2.0:94.19: Here, one dies when the five aggregates of clinging have been born and are growing;
sbh2.0:94.20: one generates defilements and, born again in the future, dies;
sbh2.0:94.21: and the falling, the falling-away of beings, the cessation of the life-faculty,
sbh2.0:94.22: the dying: this is death in its own nature.
sbh2.0:94.23: And the deva-son-māra creates obstacle for one applied to the surmounting of death,
sbh2.0:94.24: by which he is unable to surmount the death-nature,
sbh2.0:95.1: or only surmounts it after a long time.
sbh2.0:95.2: Now, the worldling free of lust by the worldly path is not under Māra’s control —
sbh2.0:96.1: whether staying here or reborn there, [he is] not under [his] control;
sbh2.0:96.2: but one who is not free of lust [is].
sbh2.0:96.3: [Of these,] the one [Conjectural: not] free of lust
sbh2.0:96.4: is as if in [his] hand, to be dealt with as he wishes.
sbh2.0:96.5: Or again, the one free of lust [by the worldly path] is bound by Māra’s bonds,
sbh2.0:96.6: not released from māra’s snares, since he must [eventually] return to this realm [of desire].
sbh2.0:96.8: When anyone’s desire for the dharma has arisen, connected with renunciation,
sbh2.0:96.9: and, making greed for sense-pleasures predominant, he [Conjectural: turns back from it] —
sbh2.0:96.10: this is to be known as a māra-action.
sbh2.0:96.11: For one dwelling with guarded sense-doors,
sbh2.0:96.12: whose mind, in lust-arousing forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, dharmas, in sign-seizing and feature-seizing, leaps forth —
sbh2.0:96.13: this is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:96.14: Likewise for one dwelling with knowledge of right measure in food, whose mind leaps forth in delight-and-lust toward exquisite tastes;
sbh2.0:96.15: or toward irregularity in eating. Likewise for one dwelling applied to wakefulness in the early and late night,
sbh2.0:96.16: whose mind leaps forth to sleeping-pleasure, lying-down-pleasure, side-lying-pleasure —
sbh2.0:96.17: this is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:96.18: Likewise for one dwelling with full awareness,
sbh2.0:96.19: in setting forth and returning etc., seeing a youthful, beautiful-complexioned, lust-arousing woman, with mind unwisely seizing the sign, leaping forth;
sbh2.0:96.20: or seeing varied worldly spectacles, mind leaps forth;
sbh2.0:96.21: in much-business, much-task, mind leaps forth —
sbh2.0:96.22: namely in delight in mixing with householders and renunciants, in being of one resolve with evil friends, and, [Conjectural: having seen them,] in approval, the mind leaps forth.
sbh2.0:96.23: This is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:97.1: Likewise toward the Buddha, dharma, saṅgha, suffering, origin, cessation, path,
sbh2.0:97.2: in this world, in the next world, doubts and indecisions arise —
sbh2.0:97.3: this is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:97.4: Gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sees a great alarming fearsomeness, terror-causing, hair-raising.
sbh2.0:97.5: In the guise of a brāhmaṇa, or of a human, or of a non-human, someone approaches, and unwisely,
sbh2.0:97.6: [Conjectural: dissuades him] from the bright side,
sbh2.0:97.7: and incites him into the dark side.
sbh2.0:97.8: This is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:97.9: When the mind leaps forth toward gain and honor,
sbh2.0:97.13: to dharmas counter to the ornament of the recluse — mind leaps forth.
sbh2.0:97.14: This is to be known as māra-action.
sbh2.0:97.15: Such are the kinds of māra-actions to be understood — those of the four māras as appropriate.
sbh2.0:98.1: Now, [Conjectural: by three] causes the undertaking of one rightly applied becomes fruitless:
sbh2.0:98.5: If the faculties are not perfected,

sbh2.0:98.15: but the concentration is weak — thus the undertaking is fruitless.

sbh2.0:98.22: by [presence of] those same three causes, [one is] fruitful.
